Virology.question: 1) The smallest DNA virus is:
Virology.exp: Parvovirus B19 is the smallest human DNA virus and is the only human DNA virus with a single-stranded genome.

Virology.question: 2) Which of the following is the largest DNA virus infecting humans?
Virology.exp: Poxviruses are the largest human viruses and replicate entirely within the cytoplasm.

Virology.question: 3) Which virus possesses a segmented RNA genome?
Virology.exp: Influenza viruses have segmented RNA genomes, allowing genetic reassortment and antigenic shift.

Virology.question: 4) Which virus is transmitted primarily through the fecal-oral route?
Virology.exp: Hepatitis A virus spreads mainly through contaminated food and water and usually causes acute self-limiting hepatitis.

Virology.question: 5) The causative agent of chickenpox is:
Virology.exp: Primary infection with varicella-zoster virus causes chickenpox, while reactivation later in life causes herpes zoster.

Virology.question: 6) Infectious mononucleosis is most commonly caused by:
Virology.exp: Epstein-Barr virus infects B lymphocytes and classically presents with fever, pharyngitis, and lymphadenopathy.

Virology.question: 7) Which virus is the most common cause of cervical cancer?
Virology.exp: Persistent infection with high-risk HPV types, especially 16 and 18, is strongly associated with cervical carcinoma.

Virology.question: 8) Which virus is the most common cause of bronchiolitis in infants?
Virology.exp: Respiratory syncytial virus is the leading cause of bronchiolitis and viral pneumonia in young children.

Virology.question: 9) Rabies is caused by a virus belonging to which family?
Virology.exp: Rabies virus is an enveloped, bullet-shaped RNA virus belonging to the family Rhabdoviridae.

Virology.question: 10) Which virus is the most common cause of hand, foot and mouth disease?
Virology.exp: Coxsackievirus A16 is the classic cause of hand, foot and mouth disease, although enterovirus 71 can also cause outbreaks.

Virology.question: 11) Which virus is the most common cause of epidemic keratoconjunctivitis?
Virology.exp: Adenovirus commonly causes epidemic keratoconjunctivitis, which spreads rapidly through direct contact and contaminated instruments.

Virology.question: 12) Which virus is the leading cause of severe gastroenteritis in infants and young children?
Virology.exp: Before widespread vaccination, rotavirus was the most common cause of severe dehydrating diarrhea in infants and young children.

Virology.question: 13) Which hepatitis virus has a defective genome and requires hepatitis B virus for replication?
Virology.exp: Hepatitis D virus depends on hepatitis B surface antigen for its assembly and transmission.

Virology.question: 14) Which virus is the principal cause of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)?
Virology.exp: HIV-1 infects CD4⁺ T lymphocytes, leading to progressive immunodeficiency and opportunistic infections.

Virology.question: 15) Which virus is the most common cause of post-transfusion hepatitis worldwide?
Virology.exp: Hepatitis C virus is efficiently transmitted through blood exposure and is a major cause of chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma.

Virology.question: 16) Which virus is the most common cause of the common cold?
Virology.exp: Rhinoviruses account for the majority of common cold cases and are transmitted mainly through respiratory droplets and direct contact.

Virology.question: 17) Which virus is the most common cause of viral croup (laryngotracheobronchitis)?
Virology.exp: Parainfluenza virus, particularly type 1, is the leading cause of croup in young children.

Virology.question: 18) Which virus is the causative agent of German measles?
Virology.exp: Rubella virus causes a mild exanthematous illness but may produce severe congenital anomalies if infection occurs during pregnancy.

Virology.question: 19) Mumps most commonly affects which organ?
Virology.exp: Mumps characteristically causes painful enlargement of the parotid glands and may also involve the testes, pancreas, and central nervous system.

Virology.question: 20) Which virus causes erythema infectiosum (fifth disease)?
Virology.exp: Parvovirus B19 causes the classic “slapped-cheek” rash in children and may trigger aplastic crisis in susceptible individuals.

Virology.question: 21) Which virus is the most common cause of congenital viral infection?
Virology.exp: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection is the most frequent congenital viral infection and a leading cause of sensorineural hearing loss.

Virology.question: 22) Which virus is the most common cause of herpangina?
Virology.exp: Coxsackievirus A commonly produces painful vesicular lesions on the soft palate and posterior oropharynx.

Virology.question: 23) Which virus is the causative agent of poliomyelitis?
Virology.exp: Poliovirus primarily infects the gastrointestinal tract and may invade anterior horn cells, resulting in acute flaccid paralysis.

Virology.question: 24) A patient develops severe encephalitis after being bitten by a rabid dog several weeks earlier. Which viral protein enables attachment of the virus to host cells?
Virology.exp: Rabies virus uses its surface glycoprotein G to bind host cell receptors and facilitate viral entry into nerve cells.

Virology.question: 25) An unvaccinated child presents with fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, and Koplik spots followed by a generalized maculopapular rash. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: Koplik spots preceding a generalized rash are pathognomonic of measles, a highly contagious infection transmitted by respiratory droplets.

Virology.question: 26) Which virus is the most common cause of epidemic viral hepatitis in developing countries?
Virology.exp: Hepatitis A spreads through the fecal-oral route and is a common cause of outbreaks related to contaminated food or water.

Virology.question: 27) Which hepatitis virus is transmitted predominantly by the fecal-oral route and is particularly severe in pregnant women?
Virology.exp: Hepatitis E usually causes an acute self-limiting illness but has a high mortality rate during the third trimester of pregnancy.

Virology.question: 28) Which virus is the most common cause of hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide?
Virology.exp: Chronic hepatitis B infection is a major risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma due to persistent hepatic inflammation and viral DNA integration.

Virology.question: 29) Which hepatitis virus has the highest likelihood of progressing to chronic infection?
Virology.exp: Most untreated hepatitis C infections become chronic and may eventually lead to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

Virology.question: 30) Which virus is the most common cause of aseptic meningitis?
Virology.exp: Enteroviruses, particularly coxsackieviruses and echoviruses, are the leading cause of viral meningitis.

Virology.question: 31) Which virus is the most common cause of viral myocarditis?
Virology.exp: Coxsackievirus B has a predilection for cardiac muscle and is a well-recognized cause of acute viral myocarditis.

Virology.question: 32) Which virus is associated with Burkitt lymphoma?
Virology.exp: Epstein-Barr virus is strongly associated with endemic Burkitt lymphoma and several other lymphoid and epithelial malignancies.

Virology.question: 33) Which virus is the causative agent of Kaposi sarcoma?
Virology.exp: Human herpesvirus 8 is the etiological agent of Kaposi sarcoma, particularly in immunocompromised individuals.

Virology.question: 34) Which virus causes roseola infantum (exanthem subitum)?
Virology.exp: Roseola typically presents with high fever followed by the appearance of a rash after the fever subsides.

Virology.question: 35) Molluscum contagiosum is caused by:
Virology.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by a poxvirus and presents as multiple flesh-colored, umbilicated papules.

Virology.question: 36) Which virus is the most common cause of recurrent herpes labialis?
Virology.exp: HSV-1 establishes latency in the trigeminal ganglion and commonly reactivates as recurrent cold sores.

Virology.question: 37) Which virus is the most common cause of genital herpes?
Virology.exp: HSV-2 is the principal cause of recurrent genital herpes, although HSV-1 may also cause genital infection.

Virology.question: 38) Which virus is responsible for oral hairy leukoplakia?
Virology.exp: Oral hairy leukoplakia is commonly seen in immunocompromised patients and is caused by Epstein-Barr virus.

Virology.question: 39) Which virus is most commonly associated with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy?
Virology.exp: JC virus reactivation in immunosuppressed individuals causes progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy through demyelination of the central nervous system.

Virology.question: 40) BK virus primarily causes disease in:
Virology.exp: BK virus may reactivate after renal transplantation, causing nephropathy and graft dysfunction.

Virology.question: 41) A patient develops painful vesicular eruptions confined to a single thoracic dermatome. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: Reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus in dorsal root ganglia causes herpes zoster with a dermatomal vesicular rash.

Virology.question: 42) A healthcare worker sustains a needle-stick injury from a patient who is HBsAg-positive. Which viral marker appearing in the blood first would indicate acute hepatitis B infection?
Virology.exp: HBsAg is the earliest detectable serological marker of acute hepatitis B infection and indicates current infection.

Virology.question: 43) A young woman has a Pap smear showing high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions. Persistent infection with which viral types is most strongly associated with this finding?
Virology.exp: HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk oncogenic types responsible for most cases of cervical carcinoma and high-grade cervical dysplasia.

Virology.question: 44) A child presents with fever, painful oral ulcers, and vesicular lesions on the palms and soles. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: Hand, foot and mouth disease is classically caused by Coxsackievirus A16, producing oral ulcers and vesicular lesions on the hands and feet.

Virology.question: 45) An HIV-positive patient develops multiple violaceous skin nodules. Which virus is most likely responsible?
Virology.exp: Human herpesvirus 8 is the etiological agent of Kaposi sarcoma, which commonly occurs in patients with advanced HIV infection.

Virology.question: 46) Which virus is the most common cause of viral encephalitis worldwide?
Virology.exp: HSV-1 is the leading cause of sporadic fatal viral encephalitis and primarily affects the temporal lobes.

Virology.question: 47) Which virus is the most common cause of nasopharyngeal carcinoma?
Virology.exp: Epstein-Barr virus is strongly associated with undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma, particularly in Southeast Asia.

Virology.question: 48) Which virus is the causative agent of severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS)?
Virology.exp: SARS-CoV is a coronavirus that caused a global outbreak of severe atypical pneumonia in 2002–2003.

Virology.question: 49) Which virus is responsible for COVID-19?
Virology.exp: SARS-CoV-2 is a novel coronavirus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic and is transmitted mainly through respiratory droplets and aerosols.

Virology.question: 50) Which virus causes Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS)?
Virology.exp: MERS-CoV is a zoonotic coronavirus associated with dromedary camels and causes severe respiratory illness with a relatively high case-fatality rate.

Virology.question: 51) Which virus is the most common cause of epidemic gastroenteritis in adults?
Virology.exp: Norovirus is highly contagious and is the leading cause of outbreaks of acute gastroenteritis in adults and closed communities.

Virology.question: 52) Which virus is classically associated with hemorrhagic cystitis in children?
Virology.exp: Certain adenovirus serotypes can cause acute hemorrhagic cystitis, particularly in children.

Virology.question: 53) Which virus is the most common cause of viral hemorrhagic fever in South Asia?
Virology.exp: Dengue virus is endemic in South Asia and is the leading cause of viral hemorrhagic fever in the region.

Virology.question: 54) Dengue virus belongs to which viral family?
Virology.exp: Dengue virus is an enveloped, positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the family Flaviviridae.

Virology.question: 55) Which mosquito is the principal vector of dengue virus?
Virology.exp: Aedes aegypti is the primary vector responsible for transmission of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses.

Virology.question: 56) Which virus is transmitted mainly by the bite of Aedes mosquitoes and is associated with congenital microcephaly?
Virology.exp: Maternal Zika virus infection during pregnancy can result in congenital Zika syndrome, including microcephaly.

Virology.question: 57) Which virus is the most common cause of Japanese encephalitis?
Virology.exp: Japanese encephalitis virus is a mosquito-borne flavivirus and an important cause of viral encephalitis in Asia.

Virology.question: 58) Which virus is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes?
Virology.exp: Culex mosquitoes are the principal vectors of Japanese encephalitis virus, with pigs and birds serving as amplifying hosts.

Virology.question: 59) Which virus is transmitted primarily by Ixodes ticks?
Virology.exp: Tick-borne encephalitis virus is transmitted by Ixodes ticks and causes meningoencephalitis in endemic regions.

Virology.question: 60) Which virus causes yellow fever?
Virology.exp: Yellow fever virus is a flavivirus transmitted by mosquitoes and can cause hepatitis, jaundice, and hemorrhagic manifestations.

Virology.question: 61) A patient develops fever, severe retro-orbital pain, myalgia, and thrombocytopenia after returning from a dengue-endemic area. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: Dengue fever classically presents with high fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia.

Virology.question: 62) A pregnant woman develops fever and a maculopapular rash after traveling to an endemic region. Fetal ultrasound later shows microcephaly. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: Congenital Zika infection is strongly associated with fetal microcephaly and other neurological abnormalities.

Virology.question: 63) A child from a rural area presents with fever, altered consciousness, and seizures during the monsoon season. Which mosquito-borne virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: Japanese encephalitis is the leading cause of epidemic viral encephalitis in many parts of Asia.

Virology.question: 64) A patient presents with fever, jaundice, renal impairment, and hemorrhagic manifestations after traveling to Africa. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: Yellow fever may progress to severe disease with jaundice, bleeding, multiorgan failure, and high mortality.

Virology.question: 65) Which viral protein of influenza virus is responsible for viral attachment to host cells?
Virology.exp: Hemagglutinin binds to sialic acid receptors on host cells, initiating viral attachment and entry.

Virology.question: 66) Influenza virus neuraminidase primarily facilitates:
Virology.option1: Release of newly formed virions from infected cells
Virology.exp: Neuraminidase cleaves sialic acid residues, allowing newly formed influenza viruses to detach from host cells and spread.

Virology.question: 67) Antigenic shift is characteristic of:
Virology.exp: Antigenic shift results from reassortment of segmented genomes and is responsible for influenza pandemics.

Virology.question: 68) Antigenic drift occurs due to:
Virology.exp: Gradual accumulation of mutations in genes encoding surface proteins leads to antigenic drift and seasonal influenza epidemics.

Virology.question: 69) Which influenza virus is responsible for most pandemics?
Virology.exp: Influenza A infects humans and animals and undergoes both antigenic drift and antigenic shift.

Virology.question: 70) Which antiviral drug inhibits influenza neuraminidase?
Virology.exp: Oseltamivir inhibits neuraminidase, reducing viral release and limiting disease progression when started early.

Virology.question: 71) Which virus is the most common cause of oral warts?
Virology.exp: Low-risk HPV types commonly produce benign papillomas and warts involving the oral cavity and skin.

Virology.question: 72) Which HPV types are most commonly associated with genital warts?
Virology.exp: HPV 6 and 11 are low-risk types responsible for the majority of anogenital warts.

Virology.question: 73) Which virus is associated with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma?
Virology.exp: HTLV-1 is an oncogenic retrovirus linked to adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma and tropical spastic paraparesis.

Virology.question: 74) Which virus is the most common cause of post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder?
Virology.exp: Impaired immune surveillance after transplantation permits uncontrolled proliferation of EBV-infected B lymphocytes.

Virology.question: 75) A patient with HIV develops painless white plaques on the lateral border of the tongue that cannot be scraped off. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: Oral hairy leukoplakia is caused by Epstein-Barr virus reactivation and is commonly seen in immunocompromised patients.

Virology.question: 76) Which virus is the most common cause of congenital cataract?
Virology.exp: Congenital rubella syndrome classically presents with cataract, congenital heart disease, and sensorineural deafness.

Virology.question: 77) Which virus is most commonly associated with congenital sensorineural hearing loss?
Virology.exp: Congenital CMV infection is the leading infectious cause of permanent sensorineural hearing loss.

Virology.question: ৭৮) Which virus is the leading cause of acute viral hepatitis worldwide?
Virology.exp: Hepatitis E is the most common cause of acute viral hepatitis globally, especially in areas with poor sanitation.

Virology.question: 79) Which hepatitis virus is not associated with chronic hepatitis?
Virology.exp: Hepatitis A causes only acute infection and does not progress to chronic hepatitis or a carrier state.

Virology.question: 80) Which virus has the longest incubation period among the hepatitis viruses?
Virology.exp: Hepatitis B has an incubation period of approximately 45–180 days, which is generally longer than that of the other common hepatitis viruses.

Virology.question: 81) Which serological marker indicates recovery and immunity following hepatitis B infection?
Virology.exp: Anti-HBs appears after clearance of HBsAg and indicates immunity following recovery or successful vaccination.

Virology.question: 82) Which hepatitis B marker is the best indicator of high infectivity?
Virology.exp: HBeAg reflects active viral replication and is associated with increased infectivity.

Virology.question: 83) Which virus is responsible for epidemic keratoconjunctivitis?
Virology.exp: Adenovirus causes highly contagious outbreaks of keratoconjunctivitis, especially in hospitals and ophthalmology clinics.

Virology.question: 84) Which virus establishes latency in the trigeminal ganglion?
Virology.exp: After primary infection, HSV-1 remains latent in the trigeminal ganglion and may reactivate as recurrent herpes labialis.

Virology.question: 85) Which virus establishes latency in the dorsal root ganglia?
Virology.exp: Varicella-zoster virus remains dormant in dorsal root or cranial nerve ganglia and reactivates as herpes zoster.

Virology.question: 86) A child presents with fever followed by painful bilateral parotid swelling. A few days later, he develops painful swelling of the testes. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: Mumps commonly affects the parotid glands and may be complicated by orchitis, especially after puberty.

Virology.question: 87) An infant develops severe bronchiolitis during winter with wheezing and respiratory distress. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: RSV is the leading cause of bronchiolitis and hospitalization for lower respiratory tract infection in infants.

Virology.question: 88) A laboratory identifies a non-enveloped DNA virus causing common warts. Which virus is the most likely pathogen?
Virology.exp: Human papillomavirus is a non-enveloped double-stranded DNA virus that causes cutaneous and mucosal warts.

Virology.question: 89) A patient with advanced HIV infection develops blurred vision. Fundoscopy reveals hemorrhagic retinal lesions with a “pizza pie” appearance. Which virus is the most likely cause?
Virology.exp: CMV retinitis is a common opportunistic infection in advanced HIV disease and is characterized by necrotizing retinitis with retinal hemorrhages.

Virology.question: 90) A healthcare worker who has completed the hepatitis B vaccination schedule is accidentally exposed to blood from an HBsAg-positive patient. Which serological marker confirms protective immunity?
Virology.exp: The presence of anti-HBs after vaccination indicates successful immune protection against hepatitis B virus infection.
